name: Argha Dey Windows Privilege Escalation Deep Dive
description: Enhanced Windows privilege escalation methodology from the Windows Privilege Escalation notes, focusing on the decision flow for the exam environment. Covers PowerUp, UAC bypass, and exploit catalog lookup.
examHabits: Run systeminfo > systeminfo.txt and check for missing patches first
Whoami /priv — always check for SeImpersonatePrivilege, SeBackupPrivilege, SeDebugPrivilege
Check if PowerShell execution is locked down — try v2, v4, or IEX from memory
winPEAS.exe output is huge — pipe to findstr to filter: winPEAS.exe quiet
Token manipulation: check who is in the local Administrators group
quickRef: systeminfo | findstr /i 'OS.Name OS.Version Hotfix'; whoami /priv; net user; net localgroup administrators

decisionPoints.action: whoami /priv — look for SeImpersonatePrivilege (JuicyPotato), SeBackupPrivilege, SeDebugPrivilege
decisionPoints.fallback: If limited, focus on file permission exploits and AlwaysInstallElevated
wmic qfe list — look for missing KB patches for known exploits

decisionPoints.action: winPEAS.exe quiet — review output for unquoted paths, weak perms, AlwaysInstallElevated

decisionPoints.condition: User has SeDebugPrivilege or local admin
decisionPoints.fallback: Check both HKLM and HKCU — if both are 1, compile a .msi to .exe payload

decisionPoints.action: PowerUp.ps1: Write-ServiceBinary — or place exe in the unquoted path directory
decisionPoints.fallback: Search manually: sc query | findstr SERVICE, then check sc qc <service> for unquoted paths

decisionPoints.condition: Service runs as SYSTEM with unquoted binary path
decisionPoints.action: PowerUp: Invoke-ServiceChange -Name '<service>' — point binary to attacker-controlled DLL
decisionPoints.fallback: Use procmon to find which DLLs load from non-existent or hijacked paths
PrintSpoofer: Spoolsample + wait — SYSTEM privilege via printer bug
Check if Spools service is running: sc query spooler

decisionPoints.action: Check for WebDav Mini-Redirector ( WebClient service ), WebDAV exploit
decisionPoints.fallback: Try NT API handle duplication or named pipe impersonation

decisionPoints.condition: Service binary is writable by current user
decisionPoints.action: Replace service executable with reverse shell payload — restart service
decisionPoints.fallback: Use PowerUp: Set-ServiceBinary — or compile custom service

decisionPoints.condition: Specific OS version with known CVEs
decisionPoints.fallback: Searchsploit or exploit-db for the kernel version

steps.phase: Phase 7 - Quick Decision Flow for the Exam

decisionPoints.condition: Exam decision tree — follow this order
decisionPoints.action: 1) AlwaysInstallElevated → 2) Unquoted Service Path → 3) DLL Hijacking → 4) SeImpersonate (JuicyPotato) → 5) Weak File/Svc Perm → 6) Kernel CVE
decisionPoints.fallback: If all fail, check for 777 scripts in scheduled tasks or writable directories in PATH
